title: Separating Solutions
subtitle: Evaporation, condensation, distillation, rectification — and what each one keeps.
objectives: Explain why dissolved substances need a different kind of method
Describe what evaporation keeps and what it throws away
Explain the role of condensation in distillation
Explain what rectification adds to simple distillation

cards.title: Nothing from the last two weeks works here
cards.text: Filters, sieves, magnets and spinning all need whole pieces. A solution has none. You have to change a state of matter instead.

cards.title: Boil the solvent off and keep the solid
cards.text: Heat the solution. The liquid leaves as gas and the dissolved solid is left behind.
points: **You keep the solute.** The solvent is gone into the air.
**Sea salt is made this way**, by sun and wind rather than a flame.
**It only works** if the solid survives being heated.
**Useless** if the liquid was the part you wanted.

cards.title: The water left. The salt did not.
cards.alt: A dry pan with a ring-shaped crust of white salt crystals left where the water evaporated
cards.text: It was dissolved, not gone. Evaporation proves a solution still had solid in it.

question.text: If salt dissolves, the salt is gone.
question.explain: It is spread through the water. Boil the water off and it is all still there.

cards.title: Two buttons
cards.text: Same heat, same flask. The difference is what you walk away with.

cards.title: Catch the gas and it turns back into liquid
cards.text: Cooling a gas back to liquid is condensation. It is the step that makes evaporation reversible.
points: **Nothing new is created.** The same molecules change state back.
**A cold surface** is all it takes — a lid, a window, a coiled tube.
**Evaporation plus condensation** is the whole trick of distillation.
**That is why** a pot lid drips.

cards.title: Why an air conditioner drips water outside
cards.text: Nobody fills it. That water came out of the air in your room, on a cold coil.
points: **Warm air holds water vapour** you cannot see.
**The cold coil** drops the air below the temperature where it can hold it.
**So it condenses** on the metal and runs off into a pipe.
**Same step as a still** — cool a vapour and you get liquid back.

question.text: You want the pure water from salty water. Which do you need?
question.explain: Evaporation alone sends the water away. You must condense it to catch it.

cards.title: The two steps, joined into one machine
cards.text: Heat the solution, pipe the vapour somewhere cold, collect what drips out. You keep the liquid this time.
points: **Boil, travel, cool, collect.** Four stages, one apparatus.
**The distillate** is what you collect. It is the pure solvent.
**Liquids with different boiling points** come off at different times.
**This is how** alcohol, perfume and fuel are separated.

cards.title: After a typhoon, this is the drinking water problem
cards.text: Floodwater is dirty and often salty. Filtering gets the mud out and does nothing about the salt.
points: **Boiling kills germs.** It does not remove salt or metals.
**Distillation removes both**, because only water leaves as vapour.
**Solar stills** do it with a sheet of plastic and sunshine.
**Know which problem you have.** Mud and salt need different answers.

question.text: Boiling floodwater makes it safe to drink even if it is salty.
question.explain: Boiling deals with germs. Salt stays behind and gets more concentrated as water leaves.

cards.title: Distilling the distillate, over and over
cards.text: One pass is rarely pure. Rectification repeats the boil-and-condense many times in a single tall column.
points: **Each cycle** leaves a little more of the unwanted liquid behind.
**A fractionating column** stacks dozens of those cycles vertically.
**Hotter at the bottom, cooler at the top**, so each height catches a different liquid.
**Crude oil refining** is this at industrial scale.

cards.title: Petrol and diesel come out of the same barrel
cards.text: Crude oil is a mixture of liquids with different boiling points. A refinery column sorts them by height.
points: **Petrol boils low**, so it rises high up the column.
**Diesel boils higher**, so it is drawn off lower down.
**Bitumen for roads** never boils and stays at the bottom.
**One mixture in, many products out**, by boiling point alone.

cards.title: Distillation keeps both halves
cards.alt: A distillation apparatus: a flask of dark liquid, a sloping condenser, and clear liquid dripping into a beaker
cards.text: The liquid dripping out is the solvent. Evaporation throws that away.

terms.def: A liquid turning to gas, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
A gas cooling back into a liquid.
Evaporating then condensing, to collect the pure liquid.
The liquid collected at the end of distillation.
Repeating distillation many times to get a purer result.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Solutions need a change of state, not a hole or a magnet.
Evaporation keeps the solid. Distillation keeps the liquid.
Condensation is the step that catches what evaporation lost.
Rectification is distillation repeated until it is pure enough.

quiz.text: Why can a filter not separate a solution?
options: Dissolved particles are smaller than any hole
quiz.explain: Dissolved means single molecules or ions. They pass through every filter.
quiz.objective: Explain why dissolved substances need a different kind of method

quiz.text: Evaporating salt water leaves you with…
quiz.explain: The water leaves as vapour. The salt stays in the dish.
quiz.objective: Describe what evaporation keeps and what it throws away

quiz.text: What does condensation do in a still?
options: Turns the vapour back into liquid so it can be collected
quiz.explain: Without the cooling step the vapour just escapes and you have plain evaporation.
quiz.objective: Explain the role of condensation in distillation

quiz.text: The liquid collected at the end of distillation is called the…
quiz.explain: Distillate. Residue and filtrate belong to filtration.
quiz.objective: Explain the role of condensation in distillation

quiz.text: Boiling salty water makes it less salty.
quiz.explain: Water leaves and salt stays, so what remains is saltier, not less.
quiz.objective: Describe what evaporation keeps and what it throws away

quiz.text: What does rectification add to a single distillation?
options: Many repeated boil-and-condense cycles for a purer result
quiz.explain: A tall column stacks dozens of cycles, so each pass removes a little more.
quiz.objective: Explain what rectification adds to simple distillation

quiz.text: In a refinery column, why is petrol drawn off higher than diesel?
options: Petrol boils at a lower temperature, so its vapour rises further
quiz.explain: Cooler near the top. A liquid condenses where the temperature matches its boiling point.
quiz.objective: Explain what rectification adds to simple distillation

quiz.text: You want drinking water from seawater. Which method?
quiz.explain: Only water leaves as vapour, so condensing it gives salt-free water.
quiz.objective: Explain why dissolved substances need a different kind of method

quiz.explain: The same molecules change state from gas back to liquid. Nothing is created.
quiz.objective: Explain the role of condensation in distillation

quiz.text: Sea salt is produced mainly by…
quiz.explain: Shallow pans, sunshine and wind. The water leaves, the salt is harvested.
quiz.objective: Describe what evaporation keeps and what it throws away

quiz.explain: Evaporate the solvent, then cool the vapour back to liquid and collect it.
quiz.objective: Explain the role of condensation in distillation

quiz.text: Bitumen stays at the bottom of a refinery column because…
options: its boiling point is far too high to vaporise
quiz.explain: It never boils at column temperatures, so it is drawn off as the heavy residue.
quiz.objective: Explain what rectification adds to simple distillation

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 4 Science. Term 1 Week 10 already distinguished evaporation from distillation, so this week adds the two parts of the scope that were not covered then — condensation as the step that makes distillation possible at all, and rectification as repeated distillation in a column. The refinery card is there because it makes rectification concrete and connects to a standing interest. The typhoon card exists to separate two problems he will otherwise merge: boiling handles germs, distillation handles dissolved salt, and knowing which you have is the actual skill.
discussion: Why does evaporation alone lose the water?
Why is the top of a refinery column cooler than the bottom?
Boiling or distilling — which do you need, and when?
extension: Put a lid on a pan of simmering salty water and taste the drips from the lid. That is distillation.
Leave a shallow dish of salt water on a windowsill for a few days.
misconceptions: That boiling removes salt. It concentrates it.
That one distillation gives something pure. Usually it does not.
